question: Should the agent-deletion journal remain a durable cross-process fence through recreation, with recreation required to claim it even after the roster entry has been removed?
rationale: This PR establishes a broad persistent lifecycle contract across config, cron, agent databases, and exec approvals; the protected maintainer label and the intended durability semantics require an explicit owner decision after the concrete recreation defect is fixed.

options.title: Fix and preserve the fencing contract
options.body: Make creation claim a completed tombstone regardless of roster-entry presence and prove delete/recreate behavior across a fresh process boundary.

options.title: Redesign the recreation handoff
options.body: Choose a different durable handoff only if maintainers intentionally want completed tombstones to stop fencing without an explicit recreation claim.

recommendation.title: Fix and preserve the fencing contract
recommendation.body: Make creation claim a completed tombstone regardless of roster-entry presence and prove delete/recreate behavior across a fresh process boundary.
